content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps: (1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). (2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. (3) sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthetic direction: target -> break amide to give acid and aniline (or amine). The amide is C(=O)N attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N). So disconnection: amide bond between carbonyl (from α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (aniline with NH2). So precursor 1: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to phenyl ring (c3ccccc3) with NH2? Wait the amide is C(=O)N attached to phenyl with NH (aniline). Actually structure: .../C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N . So carbonyl attached to N which is attached to phenyl that also has an NH (aniline). So the amide precursor: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (the part /C=C/COOH) attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N)?? Wait the unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl via the carbonyl? The SMILES: .../C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N . So the double bond attached to carbonyl carbon (C=O) which is attached to N (amide) attached to phenyl with an NH2 substituent (aniline). So the α,β-unsaturated acid precursor would be /C=C/COOH attached to phenyl? Actually the acid would be /C=C/COOH attached to phenyl? The carbonyl carbon is part of acid; after amide formation, the acid carbonyl becomes amide. So the acid precursor is /C=C/COOH attached to phenyl? The phenyl is attached to N, not to acid. So the acid precursor is the α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid) attached to phenyl? Wait cinnamic acid is Ph-CH=CH-COOH. Here we have phenyl attached to N, not to acid. So the acid is attached to phenyl? The SMILES: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 . So the aromatic ring (c2) has substituent /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. So the α,β-unsaturated acid is attached to that aromatic ring via the double bond? Actually the double bond is attached to the aromatic ring at the carbon of the double bond (the β carbon). So the substituent is a cinnamoyl amide attached to aromatic ring. So the amide formation step: break between carbonyl carbon and N, giving α,β-unsaturated acid (cinnamic acid attached to aromatic ring) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So step 1: target -> amide disconnection yields precursor A: aromatic ring with /C=C/COOH (cinnamic acid) attached; and precursor B: aniline (c3ccccc3N). Good.

Step 2: The α,β-unsaturated acid can be formed via Doebner modification from aromatic aldehyde (the same aromatic ring with aldehyde) and malonic acid. The aromatic aldehyde is the same aromatic ring (c2) with CHO group at the position where the side chain attaches. So precursor A can be disconnected to aromatic aldehyde (c2 with CHO) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). So step 2: break the C=C bond formed, giving aldehyde and malonic acid.

Step 3: The sulfonamide formation: The target also has sulfonamide linking the first aromatic ring (c1) to sulfonyl group attached to second aromatic ring (c2). So we need to disconnect sulfonamide bond to give sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) and aniline (the first aromatic ring with NH2). The first aromatic ring currently has NS(=O)(=O) attached to it; the nitrogen is attached to the first aromatic ring (c1) as an aniline (NH). So precursor C: first aromatic ring with NH2 (p-toluidine) (since there is a methyl group). So we have p-toluidine (CH3-Ph-NH2). And sulfonyl chloride derived from second aromatic ring (c2) with sulfonyl chloride attached (Ar-SO2Cl). That sulfonyl chloride also will later be used to attach to the aromatic ring after step 2? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second aromatic ring which also bears the cinnamoyl amide side chain. So after step 2 we have aromatic aldehyde (c2) with CHO and also sulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonyl chloride is on the same aromatic ring as the side chain. In the target, the sulfonyl group is attached to the second aromatic ring (c2) and the sulfonamide nitrogen attaches to first aromatic ring. So after step 3 (sulfonamide formation), we will have sulfonyl chloride attached to second aromatic ring (Ar-SO2Cl) and p-toluidine. The sulfonyl chloride also must have the side chain (cinnamoyl amide) attached later? Actually the side chain is attached to the aromatic ring via the double bond, not via the sulfonyl group. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor must already have the side chain attached (the α,β-unsaturated acid). So step 2 yields aromatic aldehyde with side chain? Wait the side chain is attached to the aromatic ring; after step 2 we have aromatic aldehyde with side chain? The side chain is the cinnamic acid attached to the aromatic ring at the position of the aldehyde? In Doebner, aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid attached to the aromatic ring (the aldehyde carbon becomes the β carbon). So the product is aromatic ring with side chain CH=CH-COOH. That's exactly precursor A (the unsaturated acid). So the sulfonyl chloride must be attached to that aromatic ring as well. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor is the same aromatic ring bearing the sulfonyl chloride and the side chain? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the aromatic ring at a different position (para to side chain). In target, the second aromatic ring has both the sulfonyl group (attached to sulfonyl chloride) and the side chain (cinnamoyl amide). So after step 2, we would have aromatic ring with sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) and side chain as unsaturated acid. So step 2 must produce that molecule: aromatic ring with sulfonyl chloride and unsaturated acid. But Doebner modification does not involve sulfonyl chloride; the sulfonyl chloride is a substituent that remains unchanged. So we need a template that forms the unsaturated acid while preserving sulfonyl chloride. The template we found earlier (reaction_id 733) is sulfonamide formation: it takes sulfonyl chloride + aniline -> sulfonamide. That matches step 3.

Thus retrosynthesis plan:

Target (T) -> step 1 (amide formation) disconnection: T -> precursor P1 (aryl sulfonamide with unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Actually after breaking amide, we get unsaturated acid attached to aromatic ring (still bearing sulfonyl chloride? No after step 1, the sulfonamide is still present, because amide is on side chain, not on sulfonamide. So P1 is the same as target but with carboxylic acid instead of amide: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1 . That's the unsaturated acid version.

Step 2 (Doebner) disconnection: P1 -> precursor P2 (aryl sulfonyl chloride with aldehyde) + malonic acid. P2 is aromatic ring with sulfonyl chloride and aldehyde (instead of side chain). SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=O)cc2)cc1? Actually aldehyde attached via CHO at same position as side chain: aromatic ring with CHO (formyl) attached. So P2: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1 . plus malonic acid.

Step 3 (sulfonamide formation) disconnection: P2 -> p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(NH2)cc1) and sulfonyl chloride aromatic (c2 with SO2Cl and aldehyde). The sulfonyl chloride aromatic is: ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2 . plus p-toluidine.

Thus we have three steps.

Now we need to retrieve template IDs for each step.

We have template 733 for sulfonamide formation (Cl-SO2-aryl + aniline -> sulfonamide). Good.

We need template for amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine -> amide). Search for amide coupling.
